situation:
You are the marketing director (participant 1) and the customer relations manager (participant 2) for TIDEWATER HARBOR SEAFOOD, a regional importer of frozen shellfish. The company sells to hotel kitchens, resorts, and independent restaurants, and it has built its reputation on the service it wraps around the product rather than on price. The president (judge) has asked the two of you to meet about a problem in the company's first out-of-state market.

TIDEWATER HARBOR SEAFOOD has supplied the same coastal region for close to fifteen years. Three months ago it opened its first territory across the state line, signing forty hospitality accounts on the strength of a guarantee the sales team promoted heavily: any product that arrives below standard is replaced within one day, at no charge and with no questions asked. That guarantee is the whole basis of the launch campaign.

Last week the company learned that a supplier had changed the vacuum pouch used for its scallop line. The new seal fails when a shipment sits above freezing for even a short time, and thawed product can spoil without any visible sign. Roughly half the pouches shipped into the new territory carry the defective seal. No customer has reported an illness, and no customer has noticed anything wrong.

Replacement stock exists, but only the volume already committed to the long-standing home accounts for next quarter. Sending it across the state line would honor the guarantee and protect the launch, and it would leave the original customers short at the height of their banquet season. The supplier cannot deliver corrected pouches for another full quarter, so that shortage would not be made up.

The other course is a public notice to every account in both markets, pulling the line and explaining the defect in the company's own words. That treats diners and both markets alike, but it spends the launch budget on recovery instead of promotion, and a larger competitor, GULFLINE PROVISIONS, is already calling on the new accounts.

The president (judge) wants your recommendation on which course to take, how the guarantee should be explained to the accounts that are affected, and what your team should say to a hospitality customer whose own guests are at stake. The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president of TIDEWATER HARBOR SEAFOOD. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked the marketing director and the customer relations manager to meet with you and recommend how the company should respond to the defective seals now in the new territory, how the replacement guarantee should be explained to the accounts affected, and what the company should say to hospitality customers who serve the product to their own guests.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant team:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up carrying the cost of the course you are recommending?
Can that be explained to the customers who carry it?
